activities.title: Establish the organizational context register
activities.description: Create a maintained view of the internal and external conditions that can influence the quality management system. Give each condition an owner and a practical review trigger.
activities.objective: Establish a current, decision-useful context register that explains which organizational conditions matter to the quality management system and why.
activities.why_it_matters: A shared view of context helps the organization set priorities that fit its real operating environment. It also makes changes easier to evaluate before they create avoidable quality or delivery risk.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Gather relevant internal conditions, external conditions, and planned changes from the people who operate and lead the business.
2. Consolidate overlapping inputs and describe the quality-management impact of each condition.
3. Assign an owner and a review trigger to each material condition.
4. Record the current response or monitoring approach where action is needed.
5. Review the register with leadership and set a recurring review cadence.
activities.expected_output: An approved organizational context register with owners, impact notes, responses, and review triggers.
activities.evidence_expectations: A maintained context register, retained review decision, and dated updates showing how relevant changes were evaluated.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Relevant internal and external conditions are explicitly recorded.
2. Each material condition has an owner.
3. The quality-management impact is understandable to process owners.
4. Review cadence and change triggers are defined.
5. Decisions and updates are retained.

activities.title: Identify interested-party planning inputs
activities.description: Identify parties that can affect or be affected by the quality management system and capture the inputs that are relevant to planning and operation.
activities.objective: Create a practical register of relevant interested parties and the quality-related needs or inputs that require attention.
activities.why_it_matters: Customer, workforce, supplier, regulatory, and community inputs can shape priorities and constraints. Separating relevant inputs from general requests keeps planning focused while preserving useful signals.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. List parties connected to the organization's products, services, processes, and operating context.
2. Identify the quality-related needs, expectations, information, or constraints each party provides.
3. Evaluate relevance to the quality management system and note the reason for the decision.
4. Assign an owner for monitoring material changes.
5. Set a periodic and change-driven review of the register.
activities.expected_output: A reviewed interested-party register with relevant inputs, ownership, and review triggers.
activities.evidence_expectations: A maintained register, review record, and examples of relevant party inputs being considered in QMS planning.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Relevant parties are identified by relationship to the organization.
2. Quality-related inputs are distinguished from general requests.
3. Relevance decisions are recorded.
4. Owners and review triggers are assigned.
5. Changes can be incorporated without rebuilding the register from scratch.

activities.title: Define the QMS scope boundaries
activities.description: Define the boundaries of the quality management system across the organization, relevant sites, products or services, processes, and functions.
activities.objective: Publish a clear and maintainable scope statement that makes the covered operating boundaries and applicability decisions understandable.
activities.why_it_matters: Clear boundaries prevent gaps in ownership and reduce confusion about which operations are managed through the QMS. A maintainable scope also gives teams a reliable reference when sites, services, or processes change.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Identify the legal or organizational boundaries included in the operating model.
2. List relevant sites, locations, products, and services.
3. Map the processes and functions that support the covered work.
4. Document applicability considerations using factual business context; do not invent exclusions.
5. Review and approve the scope with leadership, then define a change review trigger.
activities.expected_output: An approved QMS scope statement with organizational, site, product or service, process, and applicability boundaries.
activities.evidence_expectations: An approved scope statement, supporting boundary review, and retained updates when the operating model changes.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Organizational boundaries are explicit.
2. Relevant sites and locations are named.
3. Covered products or services are understandable.
4. Processes and functions are connected to the scope.
5. Applicability decisions are explained and review triggers are defined.

activities.title: Map the QMS process architecture
activities.description: Build a usable process architecture that shows how core, support, and management processes work together and how performance is understood.
activities.objective: Create a shared process architecture with clear ownership, interfaces, inputs, outputs, and performance concepts.
activities.why_it_matters: Process relationships reveal where work changes hands and where controls can be lost. A common architecture helps owners coordinate improvements without requiring a single diagramming notation.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Inventory the processes used to deliver products or services and manage the organization.
2. Classify them as core, support, or management processes.
3. Assign a process owner and describe key inputs and outputs.
4. Record important interactions, handoffs, and supporting information.
5. Identify practical performance measures or review questions for each process.
6. Review the architecture with process owners and define how it will be maintained.
activities.expected_output: A reviewed process architecture or map with process owners, interactions, inputs, outputs, and performance concepts.
activities.evidence_expectations: A maintained process map or register, owner confirmation, and retained review of significant interfaces or changes.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Core, support, and management processes are distinguishable.
2. Every included process has an owner.
3. Inputs, outputs, and key interactions are described.
4. Performance concepts are identified.
5. The architecture has a practical maintenance method.

activities.title: Confirm leadership accountability
activities.description: Make leadership involvement visible through decisions, priorities, resources, and review of quality-management performance.
activities.objective: Establish clear leadership accountability for the quality management system and the decisions needed to keep it effective.
activities.why_it_matters: Quality outcomes depend on choices about priorities, capacity, and trade-offs. Visible leadership decisions help the QMS stay connected to business direction instead of becoming a separate administrative activity.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Identify leadership decisions that influence quality performance and customer outcomes.
2. Confirm who owns those decisions and how issues are escalated.
3. Review quality objectives, risks, resources, and significant issues with leadership.
4. Record decisions, actions, and resource commitments.
5. Establish a recurring leadership review and a trigger for material changes.
activities.expected_output: A documented leadership accountability approach with decision ownership, review cadence, and retained decisions.
activities.evidence_expectations: Leadership review records, decision logs, action ownership, and evidence of resource or priority decisions.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Leadership decision rights are explicit.
2. Quality priorities are discussed with business context.
3. Significant issues have visible escalation.
4. Decisions and commitments are retained.
5. Leadership review cadence and change triggers are defined.

activities.title: Build the responsibility and authority matrix
activities.description: Define practical QMS responsibilities, authorities, and escalation paths for the decisions that affect controlled work.
activities.objective: Create a usable responsibility and authority structure that connects QMS decisions to accountable roles.
activities.why_it_matters: Unclear decision rights create delays, inconsistent responses, and hidden ownership gaps. A focused QMS matrix clarifies control decisions without duplicating the organization's full job-description system.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. List recurring QMS decisions, approvals, reviews, and escalations.
2. Assign accountable and supporting roles for each decision.
3. Define authority limits and escalation routes for unresolved issues.
4. Review the matrix with process owners and leadership.
5. Communicate the approved matrix and set a periodic suitability review.
activities.expected_output: An approved responsibility and authority matrix covering QMS decisions, approvals, reviews, and escalation routes.
activities.evidence_expectations: A maintained matrix, role-owner confirmation, and retained examples of decisions or escalations using the defined routes.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Key QMS decisions have accountable roles.
2. Authority boundaries are understandable.
3. Escalation routes are defined.
4. The matrix is communicated to affected roles.
5. Review and change mechanisms are in place.

activities.title: Set the quality policy direction
activities.description: Create or refresh a meaningful quality policy direction that connects organizational priorities, customer value, and improvement expectations.
activities.objective: Establish a concise quality policy direction that guides decisions and remains aligned with organizational strategy and quality objectives.
activities.why_it_matters: A useful policy gives people a common direction for quality decisions and improvement. Connecting it to actual priorities makes communication more credible and makes periodic review worthwhile.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Review organizational direction, customer value, and the quality outcomes the business needs.
2. Draft a concise policy direction in the organization's own language.
3. Check alignment with quality objectives and leadership priorities.
4. Approve the policy through the defined leadership decision path.
5. Communicate it to relevant people and interested parties as appropriate.
6. Set a suitability review and change trigger.
activities.expected_output: An approved quality policy direction with communication and suitability-review arrangements.
activities.evidence_expectations: The approved policy record, communication evidence, and retained periodic review or change decision.
activities.success_criteria:
1. The policy reflects organizational direction.
2. Its quality intent is understandable.
3. It supports the quality objectives.
4. Approval and communication are recorded.
5. Suitability review and change triggers are defined.

activities.title: Establish risk and opportunity planning
activities.description: Create a proportionate method for identifying and prioritizing QMS-relevant risks and opportunities, then connect decisions to actions and review.
activities.objective: Establish a practical risk and opportunity planning approach that protects intended QMS outcomes and supports improvement choices.
activities.why_it_matters: Focused risk planning helps teams act on conditions that could affect quality, customers, or process performance. A proportionate approach keeps the register useful without forcing an enterprise risk program or a single scoring method.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Identify QMS-relevant risks and opportunities from context, processes, changes, and performance results.
2. Describe potential effects and existing controls in plain operational terms.
3. Prioritize items using a method appropriate to the organization.
4. Assign actions, owners, timing, and review points for material items.
5. Integrate decisions with objectives, resources, and process reviews.
6. Reassess when conditions, performance, or planned changes warrant it.
activities.expected_output: A maintained QMS risk and opportunity register with priorities, actions, owners, and reassessment triggers.
activities.evidence_expectations: Risk and opportunity records, action follow-up, and review evidence showing reassessment after relevant changes or results.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Risks and opportunities are tied to QMS outcomes.
2. Prioritization is understandable and proportionate.
3. Material items have owners and actions.
4. Decisions connect to objectives or resources where relevant.
5. Reassessment triggers are defined.

activities.title: Deploy quality objectives
activities.description: Turn quality priorities into usable objectives with measures, targets, ownership, review cadence, and action when results move off target.
activities.objective: Create an operational quality-objective plan that supports decisions, learning, and improvement across relevant processes.
activities.why_it_matters: Objectives translate direction into work that teams can monitor and improve. Clear ownership and response rules prevent measures from becoming passive reporting with no decision path.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Select outcomes that matter to customers, processes, and organizational priorities.
2. Define the measure, baseline where useful, and target or desired condition.
3. Assign an owner and establish a review cadence.
4. Define the action or escalation path when performance is off target.
5. Confirm that the objective can be monitored with available information.
6. Review the portfolio with leadership and adjust when priorities or context change.
activities.expected_output: A quality-objective and KPI plan with measures, targets or desired conditions, owners, cadence, and response actions.
activities.evidence_expectations: Objective records, KPI definitions, review results, and retained actions or decisions for off-target performance.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Each objective describes a meaningful outcome.
2. Measures and targets or desired conditions are understandable.
3. Owners and cadence are assigned.
4. Off-target response is defined.
5. The set of objectives is reviewed against current priorities.

activities.title: Plan QMS resources
activities.description: Evaluate the people, infrastructure, tools, information, environment, monitoring resources, and capacity needed to operate and improve the QMS.
activities.objective: Establish a resource plan that connects QMS priorities to available capacity, capability, infrastructure, information, and monitoring support.
activities.why_it_matters: Resource gaps can make otherwise sound controls unreliable. A connected plan lets leadership prioritize capacity and investment based on actual QMS needs and changing workload.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Review QMS processes, objectives, risks, and planned changes for resource needs.
2. Consider people, infrastructure, tools, information, work environment, monitoring resources, and budget or capacity.
3. Compare needs with current availability and identify material gaps.
4. Assign owners, priorities, timing, and interim controls for approved actions.
5. Confirm resource decisions with leadership and affected process owners.
6. Set a review cadence and change trigger for the resource plan.
activities.expected_output: A prioritized QMS resource plan with needs, gaps, decisions, owners, and review arrangements.
activities.evidence_expectations: Resource assessment, approved priorities or capacity decisions, action follow-up, and review updates tied to QMS changes.
activities.success_criteria:
1. Resource needs are linked to QMS work and priorities.
2. Relevant resource categories are considered.
3. Gaps and interim controls are visible.
4. Decisions have owners and timing.
5. The plan is reviewed when context, workload, or performance changes.
